This is a hands-on position at the heart of the bakery's daily production. The role requires a collaborative spirit, a keen eye for detail, and a genuine passion for the art and science of baking.

· Meticulously check the quality of all raw materials and precisely weigh and measure ingredients to strict bakery formulations.

· Previous 1-2 years’ experience in a bakery, pastry kitchen, or a fast-paced culinary production environment is highly valued.

· Exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to producing consistent, high-quality work.

Benchmark Scaffolding specialises in the most complex and high-risk scaffolding projects across Australia.

Our aim is to become an extension of your company so you can leverage our business to grow your own. We are solutions focused and the delivering your project on time, on budget and safely is our highest priority.

We are seeking highly skilled and experienced RIGGERS to join our team of professionals on a full-time and permanent basis.

As a Rigger you will be responsible for assembling, installing rigging gears (such as cables, ropes, pulleys and winches), operating, and repairing rigging equipment to lift, move, and position heavy materials and machinery.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Determine the necessary type and size of rigging gear, and inspect and prepare the appropriate rigging gear/equipment for the task before use and ensure compliance with safety regulations
Attach rigging gear to equipment, structural steel or other heavy objects
Communicate with operators and crew to guide load movement and ensure safe execution
Build and dismantle rigging equipment and hoists
Use mechanical load shifting equipment and associated tools, such as winches, hoists and other lifting equipment, to lift, lower, move, position and secure objects
Maintain and repair rigging gear
Record completed work orders and report issues or hazards

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Minimum 3 years working experience as a Rigger or in the same field
In-depth knowledge of rigging equipment, machinery, and safety protocols is essential. This includes the ability to perform load calculations
As this job is physically demanding, you must have physical strength and the ability required to lift heavy equipment and work long hours in various weather conditions and at heights
Strong communication, problem-solving, and spatial awareness
Ability to work well both independently and in a team environment
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

Apprentice Mobile Plant Mechanic  
    
 Programmed Apprenticeships & Traineeships, in partnership with Leichhardt, is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Apprentice Mobile Plant Mechanic to join the team at the Lake MacLeod operation in Carnarvon, Western Australia. 
  
  Build Your Future with Leichhardt  
 If you are mechanically minded and ready to commence a hands-on career in heavy machinery, this is your opportunity to learn from experienced tradespeople while earning a nationally recognised qualification. 
  
  What's on Offer  
 
 Full-time paid apprenticeship 
 Hands-on training and the opportunity to work on a range of mobile plant and heavy equipment including loaders, excavators, and trucks 
 Mentoring and support from experienced Mechanics 
 A safe, supportive and team-focused workplace 
 The opportunity to build a long-term career in the mining and resources industry 
 
  
  About You  
 We're looking for someone who: 
 
 Has a genuine interest in mechanics and heavy machinery 
 Is reliable, motivated and eager to learn 
 Can work effectively both independently and as part of a team 
 Is committed to working safely and maintaining a positive attitude 
 Is willing to follow instructions, take initiative and continually develop new skills 
 Has completed Year 10 or equivalent (preferred), with sound mathematics skills 
 Holds a current driver's licence or is working towards obtaining one 
 
  
  What You'll Learn  
 As an Apprentice Mobile Plant Mechanic, you'll gain valuable hands-on experience while developing the practical skills needed to become a qualified tradesperson. Throughout your apprenticeship, you'll learn how to: 
 
 Diagnose faults and carry out mechanical repairs, component removals and installations 
 Inspect, maintain and repair braking, steering, cooling and suspension systems 
 Service and maintain fixed and mobile plant equipment to manufacturer and workplace standards 
 Assemble, fit, clean and lubricate mechanical components using a range of tools and equipment 
 Diagnose and repair low-voltage (12V and 24V) electrical systems 
 Prepare new machinery and equipment for commissioning and operation 
 Perform scheduled servicing and preventative maintenance 
 Rebuild machines and major mechanical components 
 Diagnose and repair hydraulic systems and faults 
 Read and interpret technical manuals, service information and workshop documentation 
 Work safely in accordance with company procedures, policies and industry standards 
 Communicate effectively with supervisors, qualified tradespeople and other team members 
 Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the workshop 
 Successfully balance on-the-job training with TAFE studies to complete your apprenticeship 
 
  
  Why Choose Leichhardt?  
 Leichhardt is committed to developing the next generation of skilled tradespeople. You'll gain valuable hands-on experience, receive quality mentoring, and work in an environment that values safety, teamwork and professional development. 
  
  What You Need to Know Before Applying  
 This apprenticeship may require you to attend TAFE in Perth several times throughout the year under a block-release training model. During these periods, travel and accommodation will be arranged and paid for by the company; however, attendance is compulsory. 
  
 You should be comfortable: 
  
 
 Living away from home for short periods while attending TAFE block release (generally up to two weeks at a time) 
 Travelling independently to and from Perth, including between your arranged accommodation and TAFE each day 
 Committing to both your workplace responsibilities and training requirements throughout the duration of your traineeship 
 
  
 This is an important part of successfully completing your nationally recognised qualification. 
  
  If you're ready to start your career as an Apprentice Mobile Plant Mechanic, we'd love to hear from you.  
  
  Location:  Carnarvon, WA  Position:  Full-Time Apprenticeship  Start Date:  Early 2027  Applications close:  Friday, 28 August 2026 
    
  Please note: Programmed reserves the right to close applications before the advertised closing date.  
  
  Who we are  
 As one of Australia's largest employers, we work with great companies all around Australia and New Zealand to give you the best opportunities to work when and where you want to. 
 At Programmed, we are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment which values and respects diverse styles, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. 
 We welcome and encourage women, people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent and people from diverse backgrounds to apply. 
   So it's over to you. If you would like to join our team, APPLY now.
